originalTitle: Berkshire Hathaway Just Did Something It Hasn’t Done in More Than 3 Years
summary: For three years, Greg Abel sat on one of the largest cash piles in corporate history while the market ran without him. Something just changed, and the new portfolio bets reveal exactly where Berkshire is placing its next big wager.
content:
Berkshire Hathaway ( NYSE:BRK-A | BRK-A Price Prediction )( NYSE:BRK-B ) has been the poster child for that patience — building the largest cash pile in its history rather than chasing a market that Warren Buffett openly said he found too expensive. That patience just ended.

Berkshire ended the first quarter of 2026 with $397.4 billion in cash and Treasury bills , a record and the culmination of a strategy Buffett began years earlier and Greg Abel continued after taking over as CEO on January 1. Between 2022 and 2024 alone, Berkshire sold a net $172.9 billion more in stocks than it bought. That selling didn’t stop when Abel took the reins — it accelerated into a streak of 14 consecutive quarters as a net seller of equities , one of the longest such stretches in Berkshire’s history.

This morning’s second-quarter earnings release broke that streak. Berkshire’s cash position fell to $365.5 billion, and for the first time in more than three years, Abel was a net buyer of stocks — purchasing roughly $20 billion more in equities than he sold. Berkshire also stepped up share buybacks to $4.5 billion for the quarter, a sharp jump from the token $235 million spent in Q1.

Greg Abel just ended Berkshire's 14-quarter selling streak. The $397 billion war chest is finally moving into a massive new growth bet. © 24/7 Wall St.

Apple’s Shrinking Shadow, and a New Favorite Emerges

The portfolio shift shows up most clearly in what Berkshire owns. Apple ( NASDAQ:AAPL ) once accounted for more than half of Berkshire’s equity portfolio at its peak. Today, Apple represents just 20% of the $355 billion portfolio — still the largest position, but no longer the dominant one. Bank of America ( NYSE:BAC ) tells a similar story in reverse gear. Buffett left the stock untouched for years after first buying it in 2011, watching it grow into his second-largest holding. Since the middle of 2024, Berkshire has cut the position nearly in half, offloading roughly 519 million shares. Bank of America now sits at $32.49 billion, or 9.1% of the portfolio — Berkshire’s fourth-largest position.

Alphabet is the newest name on that list, and it didn’t get there by accident. Berkshire revealed a $10 billion investment in Alphabet earlier this year , earmarked to help fund the company’s AI infrastructure buildout, and it’s fast becoming an Abel favorite. Berkshire’s Alphabet stake grew 224% in Abel’s first quarter alone, expanding from 17.8 million shares at the end of 2025 to nearly 58 million shares in Q1. Buffett has said he personally initiated the position, but Abel is the one who decided how far to run with it.

Granted, one quarter of net buying doesn’t undo three years of net selling — Berkshire still holds $365.5 billion in dry powder, plenty to fund another Alphabet-sized bet or absorb a real market pullback. That said, the signal here matters more than its size. Abel has shown he’ll deploy capital when he sees value, and Alphabet’s rise into the top five holdings — alongside a stepped-up buyback pace — suggests he’s done waiting.

For shareholders, that’s the clearest sign yet that Berkshire’s multiyear defensive crouch is giving way to something more offensive. In the end, that’s a reason for smart investors to keep paying attention to what Abel buys next.

chineseTitle: 伯克希尔哈撒韦公司刚刚做了三年多来没有做过的事情
chineseSummary: 三年来，格雷格·阿贝尔坐拥公司历史上最大的现金储备之一，而市场却在没有他的情况下运转。事情刚刚发生了变化，新的投资组合押注准确地揭示了伯克希尔下一笔大赌注的方向。
chineseContent:
伯克希尔·哈撒韦公司 (NYSE:BRK-A | BRK-A 价格预测)(NYSE:BRK-B) 一直是这种耐心的典型代表——建立其历史上最大的现金储备，而不是追逐沃伦·巴菲特公开表示他认为太昂贵的市场。那种耐心刚刚结束。

伯克希尔哈撒韦公司截至 2026 年第一季度的现金和国库券为 3,974 亿美元，创历史新高，也是巴菲特多年前开始、格雷格·阿贝尔 (Greg Abel) 在 1 月 1 日接任首席执行官后继续推行的战略的顶峰。仅在 2022 年至 2024 年期间，伯克希尔哈撒韦公司卖出的股票就比买入的股票净多了 1,729 亿美元。当阿贝尔上任后，这种抛售并没有停止——它连续 14 个季度连续净抛售股票，这是伯克希尔历史上最长的连续抛售之一。

今天早上发布的第二季度财报打破了这一连续纪录。伯克希尔哈撒韦的现金头寸降至 3655 亿美元，三年多来，阿贝尔首次成为股票净买家——购买的股票比卖出的股票多了约 200 亿美元。伯克希尔本季度还将股票回购力度加大至 45 亿美元，较第一季度象征性的 2.35 亿美元大幅增加。

格雷格·阿贝尔刚刚结束了伯克希尔哈撒韦公司连续 14 个季度的抛售。 3,970 亿美元的资金终于投入到新的大规模增长投资中。 © 24/7 华尔街

苹果的影子缩小，新宠出现

投资组合的转变在伯克希尔所拥有的资产中体现得最为明显。苹果（NASDAQ：AAPL）在巅峰时期曾占伯克希尔股票投资组合的一半以上。如今，苹果公司仅占 3550 亿美元投资组合的 20%——仍然是最大的位置，但不再占据主导地位。美国银行（NYSE：BAC）也讲述了类似的故事。巴菲特在 2011 年首次购买该股票后，多年来一直没有动过该股票，看着它成长为他的第二大持股。自 2024 年中期以来，伯克希尔已将持仓量削减近一半，抛售约 5.19 亿股。美国银行目前的资产为 324.9 亿美元，占投资组合的 9.1%，是伯克希尔的第四大资产。

Alphabet 是该名单上最新的名字，它的出现并非偶然。伯克希尔哈撒韦公司今年早些时候透露了对 Alphabet 的 100 亿美元投资，专门用于为该公司的人工智能基础设施建设提供资金，它很快就成为阿贝尔的最爱。仅在阿贝尔第一季度，伯克希尔所持有的 Alphabet 股份就增长了 224%，从 2025 年底的 1780 万股增加到第一季度的近 5800 万股。巴菲特曾表示，他亲自发起了这一职位，但阿贝尔才是决定该职位走多远的人。

诚然，四分之一的净买入并不能消除三年来的净卖出——伯克希尔仍然持有 3655 亿美元的干粉，足以为另一笔 Alphabet 规模的赌注提供资金或吸收真正的市场回调。也就是说，这里的信号比它的大小更重要。阿贝尔已经表明，当他看到价值时，他会配置资本，而 Alphabet 跻身前五名持股公司——同时回购步伐加快——表明他已经不再等待。

对于股东来说，这是迄今为止最明显的迹象，表明伯克希尔多年来的防御性蹲伏正在让位于更具进攻性的东西。最后，这就是聪明的投资者继续关注阿贝尔下一步购买什么的原因。
